issues.description: Returning nil from run() relocates the nil-deref upstream instead of fixing it
issues.detail: When CompareAndSwap fails and t.result.Load() is nil, run() returns bare nil, breaking the previously universal postcondition that run() yields a non-nil *result. Every caller downstream must now handle nil where one was guaranteed. The leader-panic-cleanup path should produce a sentinel *result with Fatal set and a closed done channel, not a nil escape hatch.

issues.description: Overloading nil in t.result is the wrong data structure for leader-failure
issues.detail: t.result (atomic *result) now encodes three distinct facts via the same nil sentinel: not-started, leader-panicked-cleanup, and waiter-should-bail. This place-oriented overload is what made the race surface. Storing a failed-result value with Fatal set and a pre-closed done channel would close the race by construction and let waitUntilDone work uniformly, deleting the new nil-check branch.

issues.description: Cycle check skipped on the CAS-failure slow path where it previously ran
issues.detail: Previously checkCycle ran whenever t.result.Load() was non-nil at entry. After the refactor, when CAS fails because another goroutine became leader, control jumps straight to waitUntilDone with no checkCycle call. A caller in a cycle that races into this branch will deadlock on output.done instead of erroring with ErrCycle. Reinstate the cycle check on the slow path.

issues.description: Comment inverts the meaning of the panic-recovery branch
issues.detail: The comment reads 'Leader panicked but we did see a result' but the branch fires precisely when output is nil — i.e. we did NOT see a result. Comments are part of the spec; an inverted comment on a subtle concurrency branch will mislead future maintainers about when this path fires and whether returning nil is intended.

issues.description: Leader-panic invariant and new waitUntilDone snapshot contract are undocumented
issues.detail: The fix depends on an invariant — when the leader panics it CASes t.result back to nil — that lives in cleanup code and is invisible at the run() call site. Similarly, waitUntilDone's new *result parameter changes its contract to wait on the caller-supplied snapshot, not whatever t.result currently advertises. Both invariants need to be documented at the type boundary so future edits don't silently break them.

issues.description: No test reproduces the leader-panic race; the fix is unverified
issues.detail: The diff adds no test exercising the leader-panic-then-waiter-reads-nil path. A race fix without a race test is folklore. A small test that panics the leader goroutine and asserts the waiter neither derefs nil nor deadlocks would lock in the invariant and document the intended behavior.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the cycle-check extraction and passing *result explicitly into waitUntilDone are clean wins that remove the TOCTOU window. But the core fix is judged unsound: returning bare nil from run() breaks a universal postcondition and just relocates the nil-deref one frame up. The root cause is overloading nil in t.result to encode multiple distinct states; the correct fix is to store a failed-result sentinel with Fatal set and a closed done channel on leader panic. Additionally, the cycle check is now skipped on the CAS-failure path, a comment inverts the actual semantics, key invariants are undocumented, and no test reproduces the race.
